text: A gilt's first estrus cycle appears around 6 months of age. In sows, a new estrus appears 5–7 days after weaning piglets; if the sow is very thin, estrus can be delayed for weeks until she regains condition. If a sow or gilt is not mated or inseminated, a new cycle appears 21 days later. Estrus is easier to detect with a boar nearby — nose-to-nose contact makes the sow raise her ears and the boar become active. A second sign is a swollen, reddened vulva, though this can be subtle. The most reliable sign is immobility: if the farmer sits on the sow's or gilt's back, an animal in standing heat will stay still. The best window for mating or insemination is 12 to 24 hours after these signs appear.
